title: Matched control: the fixed-depth baseline is seed-reliable where the adaptive one is not
why_this_was_run: QNEURO3-Q3-VARIANCE-001 found that Q3 reaches its headline result on 6 of 10 seeds. That
number is meaningless on its own -- the task, the optimiser or the training budget could be
flaky for every architecture. The comparison only becomes interpretable against the baseline
Q3 is being sold against, run under identical conditions.

design.architecture: Q0Fixed at depth 8, 28360 parameters, the same Core as Q3
design.held_fixed: AdamW lr 2e-3, 8 epochs, batch 128, 500 batches, grad-norm clip 1.0, 24 nodes, d=64, identical frozen validation set per task

finding: Q0 reaches accuracy >= 0.99 on 10 of 10 seeds across both task constructions, with a minimum
of 0.9919. The task is not flaky, the optimiser is not flaky, and the training budget is
sufficient. The unreliability measured in QNEURO3-Q3-VARIANCE-001 is a property of the
Note that Q0 is 5 of 5 on chase_to_goal_weighted, where Q3 was 1 of 10. The task-construction
gap (finding V4) therefore also belongs to Q3 and not to the task.

the_comparison_this_forces.adaptive_depth_Q3: 0.9994-1.0000 accuracy at 4.54 steps on 6 of 10 seeds; 0.42-0.51 at 5.6-6.0 steps on 4 of 10
honest_reading: Q3 buys a 1.77x inference-compute reduction in exchange for a 40% chance of a silently
broken model, against a baseline that never breaks. Expected accuracy across seeds is 0.78
for Q3 against 1.00 for Q0. On the axis a user actually cares about -- 'will the model I
train work' -- adaptive depth loses outright here.
This does not say adaptive depth cannot win somewhere. It says that on this task, at this
scale, with this training budget, it does not, and that the 1.77x figure is not reportable
